e: enable secret hashes the privileged-mode password; enable password stores it in cleartext
d: If both are configured, enable password is ignored — always use enable secret.

e: copy running-config startup-config saves to NVRAM (write is the old-style equivalent)
d: write erase or erase startup-config / erase nvram factory-resets the device by clearing NVRAM.

e: The 16 virtual terminal lines used for both Telnet and SSH access to the CLI
d: Configuring login/password or login local under this context secures remote CLI access.

e: Requires hostname + ip domain-name (to form an FQDN), crypto key generate rsa, local usernames, and ip ssh version 2
d: transport input ssh under the VTY lines enables SSH and disables Telnet.

e: A Layer 2 switch's logical interface, associated with a VLAN, used for administrative access
d: A Layer 2 switch can have only one IP address (on one SVI) for management. A Layer 3 switch can have multiple IP addresses across SVIs and routed physical ports.

e: ip address dhcp on an SVI has the switch obtain its management IP automatically
d: show dhcp lease shows DHCP leases on all SVIs.

e: show history displays exec command history
d: terminal history size x sets history size for the current session only; (config)# history size x sets the default.

e: Synchronises unsolicited syslog messages with other console output
d: Configured under (config-line) for a given line so messages don't interrupt command entry mid-type.

e: Logs out a user after a set period of inactivity
d: Default is 5 minutes; exec-timeout 0 0 disables the timeout entirely.

e: Stops the device from trying to resolve what looks like a domain name in the command line
d: Without this, a mistyped command can hang for a DNS lookup timeout before erroring.

e: Auto-negotiation is disabled only if both speed and duplex are set manually on a port
d: If the other side has auto-negotiation disabled, IEEE standard requires matching the slowest supported speed and, at 10/100 Mbps, half-duplex. Cisco instead senses speed and uses full duplex at 1000 Mbps+.

e: Line status down, protocol status down
d: Shown by "show interfaces status" as notconnect — cable not connected or faulty.
Caused by port security, DHCP Snooping, Dynamic ARP Inspection, or another security mechanism disabling the interface.

e: Line and protocol status both administratively down
d: Caused by the shutdown command being applied to the interface.

t: Ethernet input errors — runts and giants
e: Runts are frames smaller than 64 bytes, often caused by collisions
d: Giants are frames larger than the standard 1518-byte maximum; frames up to 1600 bytes (e.g. from 802.1Q-in-802.1Q or MPLS) are valid "baby giants", and deliberately larger frames up to 9000 bytes are "jumbo frames".

e: Frames that fail the Frame Check Sequence

t: Ethernet output errors — collisions and late collisions
e: Collisions counts all collisions detected while transmitting a frame
d: Late collisions — happening after the frame's 64th byte — signal a duplex mismatch, since in half-duplex mode collisions should be detected before the 64th byte.

e: Shows all dynamically learned MAC addresses
d: Can be filtered with "address AAAA.BBBB.CCCC" (Cisco's 3-quartet MAC format), "interface Gi0/0", or "vlan 1".

e: Shows the global (or per-VLAN) MAC address ageing timer setting
d: show mac address-table count shows used and available space in the MAC address table.
